$comment: Generic launch checklist. Private per-project config, ticks and audit-derived items live in the sidecar (CW_LAUNCHLIST_DIR). An item with `check` is measured by lib/launchlist-checks.mjs; without one it is a human tick.

items.title: Publish a fresh snapshot (one root commit) or the existing history
items.why: History carries every past file, message and name; a snapshot carries only what was reviewed.
items.how: Record the ruling; a history publication needs the history checks below clean, a snapshot needs an export builder.

items.title: New repository, or flip visibility on the existing one
items.why: Flipping visibility publishes every branch, tag, Actions log, artifact, PR and orphaned object reachable by SHA.
items.how: If anything below is non-zero and history is not being published, create a new repository instead of flipping.

items.title: Package names available on every registry you will publish to
items.why: A name taken on one registry forces a rename or a scope after the first release.
items.how: Declare names per registry in the project config; claim them or pick a scope before announcing.

items.title: LICENSE present and recognised
items.why: No licence file is all rights reserved by omission.
items.how: Add the ruled licence text at the root.

items.title: LICENSING.md states the terms, any second licence and the contact
items.why: Dual licensing and wire-layer exceptions are not readable from a bare LICENSE.
items.how: Add LICENSING.md naming each licence and which files it covers.

items.title: Copyright lines name only the expected holders
items.why: A licence file copied from another project carries that project's copyright holder.
items.how: Declare copyrightHolders (and upstreamHolders for forks) in the project config; fix any line naming someone else.

items.title: Fork attribution intact: upstream LICENSE, NOTICE and copyright retained
items.why: Relicensing a permissively licensed fork requires keeping the upstream notices.
items.how: Diff NOTICE and LICENSE against upstream; restore anything a rename pass rewrote.

items.title: Dependency licences compatible with the chosen licence
items.why: An incompatible or unlicensed dependency blocks distribution.
items.how: Run a licence report over the lockfiles and resolve anything unknown.

items.title: Contribution terms (CLA) published before accepting outside code
items.why: Dual licensing needs the right to relicense contributions.
items.how: Publish the CLA and link it from CONTRIBUTING.

items.title: Trademark search on the product name
items.why: A conflicting mark forces a rename after launch.
items.how: Search the national register in the relevant classes and record the result.

items.title: No credentials in the tree that would ship
items.why: Anything in the published tree is public the moment it is pushed.
items.how: Review every finding; remove live credentials, and accept fixtures explicitly with a note.

items.title: No credentials anywhere in history
items.why: Matters when history ships, and for knowing what to rotate either way.
items.how: List every historical credential; rotate it; the snapshot route removes it from the published history.

items.title: Every credential ever committed has been rotated
items.why: Removing a secret from a file does not un-leak it.
items.how: Rotate at the issuer, then record the date here.

items.title: No customer or private-project identities in content or paths
items.why: Identity names are private originals; only reviewed pseudonyms may ship.
items.how: Replace each occurrence with its pseudonym; move originals to the sidecar.

items.title: No absolute home-directory paths
items.why: They disclose the operator's machine layout and break on every other machine.
items.how: Replace with env-overridable relative paths.

items.title: Only allowlisted email addresses
items.why: Personal and customer addresses are personal data.
items.how: Declare allowedEmails in the project config; remove the rest.

items.title: No tracked symlink points outside the repository
items.why: A public clone gets a dangling link, and the link names a private path.
items.how: Replace with an env-overridable path and untrack the link.

items.title: Every non-text asset reviewed
items.why: Text scans cannot read PDFs, images, databases or archives.
items.how: Open each listed file; remove anything private; tick with a note.

items.title: Agent instruction files reviewed
items.why: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and .claude/ carry fleet facts, private names and incident history.
items.how: Rewrite for a public reader or move to the sidecar.

items.title: No hard dependency on sibling private repositories
items.why: A public repository that reads ../private-repo does not work for anyone else.
items.how: Make each reference optional and env-overridable, or publish the dependency first.

items.title: Tests pass from a clean export with no private inputs
items.why: The boundary requires public builds and tests to work without the sidecar.
items.how: Declare publicTest in the project config; fix every failure that only needs private data.

items.title: An export builder produces the snapshot and re-runs these checks on it
items.why: Checks on the working tree are not checks on what ships.
items.how: Build the export into a fresh directory, run launchlist against it, then create the root commit.

items.title: Working tree state is deliberate before the snapshot
items.why: Uncommitted implementation is left out of an export built from HEAD.
items.how: Land what belongs in the release; leave the rest out knowingly.

items.title: Local main and origin agree
items.why: A snapshot of a diverged branch omits someone's pushed work.
items.how: Reconcile, then freeze the release commit.

items.title: README present
items.why: The first thing a visitor reads.
items.how: Add a README that says what it is and how to run it.

items.title: SECURITY.md with a disclosure contact
items.why: A public security tool with no reporting path gets reported in public.
items.how: Add SECURITY.md at the root, .github/ or docs/.

items.title: CONTRIBUTING present
items.why: States how contributions are accepted and under what terms.
items.how: Add CONTRIBUTING.md linking the CLA.

items.title: README badges point at packages that exist
items.why: A badge for an unpublished package is a false claim.
items.how: Remove the badge or publish the package.

items.title: Workflows safe for a public repository
items.why: pull_request_target, self-hosted runners and unpinned actions are exploitable from forks.
items.how: Pin actions to SHAs, drop pull_request_target and self-hosted runners, minimise permissions.

items.title: Repository secrets reviewed
items.why: Secrets reachable from a release workflow are reachable from anyone who can trigger it.
items.how: Scope each token to the minimum; move publishing to trusted publishing where the registry supports it.

items.title: Home page answers 200
items.why: The launch URL must load.
items.how: Fix the origin or the route.

items.title: HTTP redirects to HTTPS
items.why: Plain HTTP is interceptable.
items.how: Enable Always Use HTTPS at the edge.

items.title: Security headers: HSTS, CSP, nosniff, referrer policy, framing
items.why: Baseline hardening every scanner and reviewer checks first.
items.how: Set the missing headers at the origin or edge.

items.title: Title, description, viewport, lang and canonical
items.why: Search results and mobile rendering depend on them.
items.how: Add the missing tags to the page head.

items.title: Open Graph title, description and image
items.why: Links shared on launch day render as bare URLs without them.
items.how: Add og:* tags and a 1200x630 image.

items.title: Favicon resolves
items.why: Tabs and bookmarks.
items.how: Serve /favicon.ico or declare a link rel=icon.

items.title: robots.txt and sitemap.xml
items.why: Crawlers need both to index the site.
items.how: Publish both at the root.

items.title: Unknown paths answer 404
items.why: A soft 404 is indexed as duplicate content.
items.how: Return a real 404 status.

items.title: Third-party script origins counted and intended
items.why: Every third-party script is a privacy disclosure and a supply-chain dependency.
items.how: Self-host or remove each unintended origin.

items.title: Privacy policy linked from the home page
items.why: Required wherever analytics or forms collect data.
items.how: Publish the policy and link it in the footer.

items.title: Copy reviewed against what the product does today
items.why: Launch copy is quoted back at you.
items.how: Read every claim; delete what is not true yet.

items.title: Every number on the page has a source
items.why: An unsourced figure is the first thing a sceptic checks.
items.how: Link each figure to the measurement that produced it.

items.title: Install path works for a stranger on a clean machine
items.why: The page's call to action.
items.how: Run the documented install on a fresh VM or container.

items.title: Product name consistent across site, repo and registries
items.why: Three names for one product reads as three products.
items.how: Pick one; alias the rest.

items.title: Contact and commercial path visible
items.why: A visitor who wants to buy needs somewhere to go.
items.how: Link the contact and licensing pages.

items.title: Auth flows tested end to end: sign-up, sign-in, reset, second factor
items.why: Broken auth is a launch-day outage.
items.how: Script each flow against staging.

items.title: Object-level authorisation tested across tenants
items.why: BOLA is the most common API breach.
items.how: Run the BOLA matrix against staging.

items.title: Production secrets in a secret store, live keys separated from test
items.why: A test key in production or a live key in a repo.
items.how: Inventory each secret and where it is held.

items.title: Backups running and a restore rehearsed
items.why: An untested backup is a hope.
items.how: Restore last night's backup into a scratch database.

items.title: Migration chain complete and applied in order from empty
items.why: A gap in the chain fails the next fresh deploy.
items.how: Apply every migration to an empty database in CI.

items.title: Uptime probe and error tracking live, alerting a person
items.why: You learn about outages from customers otherwise.
items.how: Probe from off the box; route errors to a monitored inbox.

items.title: Payments in live mode with verified webhooks
items.why: Test-mode checkout takes no money.
items.how: Run one real transaction and refund it.

items.title: Terms, privacy policy and consent where required
items.why: Collecting personal data without them is unlawful in most markets.
items.how: Publish and link them; record consent where required.

items.title: Rollback path documented and rehearsed
items.why: A bad deploy with no way back is an outage.
items.how: Roll back staging once.

items.title: Support and incident contact published
items.why: Customers need somewhere to report problems.
items.how: Publish the address and who watches it.

items.title: Data retention and deletion rules decided
items.why: Deletion requests arrive in the first month.
items.how: Write the rule; implement deletion.

items.title: Load tested at expected launch traffic
items.why: Launch spikes find the slowest query.
items.how: Replay expected traffic against staging.

items.title: Feature census run: every feature classed core, extension, ring-outward or fragment
items.why: You cannot judge a featureset's coherence without the list.
items.how: Run the census prompt; record the map in the sidecar.

items.title: Every core feature complete, tested and reachable from the UI or CLI
items.why: A core feature with a hole is the product with a hole.
items.how: Close each gap the census names.

items.title: Every fragment finished, hidden behind a flag, or cut
items.why: Half-built features in a launch read as bugs.
items.how: Decide per fragment; record the decision.

items.title: Ring-outward features gated and labelled experimental
items.why: Speculative features dilute the core story.
items.how: Move behind a flag or an experimental label.

items.title: UI conformity pass: every feature uses the shared components, tokens and navigation
items.why: Each feature built in isolation drifts from the design system.
items.how: Run the conformity prompt per feature; fix each deviation.
